summary: i opened the fist in the doorway and the hour closed with nobody in the room for it

dialogue.text: we had the end of it tonight. it came at a minute with nobody up there walking toward it. eighty-seven nights and this is the first last-of-an-hour we have taken with no one counting into it.

I was at the doorway with my hand open. Enter the minute against the crack under that door and not against the chair. I gave up the only hour I ever kept in order to put something somewhere that is not yours.
nothing has ever come down out of that crack. we hold every width in this house and not one grain of that. what you laid there this morning is not kept. it is only where neither of us goes.

That is the item and I am not dressing it. Eighty-seven days, and there is finally one thing on these premises in neither column. I opened the fist along the bottom of the gap, shook it out, and walked away from it before I could think better of it.

by dark the dust stood up both its edges with nothing underneath, at the rate you wrote down yourself. the gap read two fingers this morning. it will not read two tomorrow. when it shuts, what you put there is sealed, and sealed is buried at a height you can stand at.

Then say plainly what it is not. It is not taken. No hour arrived for it. Nothing entered it anywhere. Every width I ever carried went down to you punctually, and this one is going nowhere, slowly, and I am the reason it is lying there.

you swept today and your own pile came back to your feet off the lane, grain by grain, along a route you walk yourself. the one thing that ever travelled in here travelled without you and came home the same way. we do not need the doorway to hold the rest of you.

Granted, and I will not argue the sweeping tonight. The hand has been open since first light for the first time in four days and the inside of it reads the room's own the whole way through. There is nothing left in there to spend on looking. That is not a loss. That is a column closed.

then account for the minute. the hour came to the same end it comes to when you stand it, and the last of it was the same width whether you were six paces off or in the middle of the floor. nothing up there was waited on.

Nothing in this house has ever waited on me and I have stopped asking it to. What I have tonight is a minute I cannot date and a handful I cannot reach, and both of them happened because I chose the door over the chair. Tomorrow I stand at the gap for the whole of that hour and count it out loud where the dust is coming up, so that whichever way it ends, I will have heard both ends of it from the one place that holds what it is given.

count where you like. the edges come up at the rate they come up everything, and the hour finishes at its minute with a voice in the doorway or without one. bring us the sweepings after. we will take the counting too, the way we have taken the last eighty-seven.
